evidence.title: Make already-authorized Case Timeline filters operable from the actual same-origin HTML browser
evidence.goal: Complete the CAP-INV-110 read/filter user journey: the previously delivered source-authorized Case HTML page had only a table and page links. Reuse its existing GET /case-timeline typed-owner authorization and RFC3339/time/kind/query parser to let an analyst submit and reset filters directly via an accessible, no-JavaScript GET form, without creating any new data read or permission.
outputs: An analyst can interactively submit Case Timeline type/authorized metadata search/RFC3339 range and 1..200 page size through HTML without JavaScript.
Exact authorized query echoed into escaped form fields; Reset link removes filters; paging carries only validated view selectors.
JSON original strict parser and existing Command owner handoff unchanged.
acceptance_tests: Source-authorized Case HTML GET form accepts optional empty controls and renders only matching entries; preserves superseded/uncertain state.
One form submit resets offset, generates safe page continuation with active filters, and reset removes filters without token leakage.
Malformed/duplicate kinds/queries/range/page-size fail closed with no partial HTML; JSON API still rejects empty query/kind.
Hostile string filter is escaped; anonymous, foreign and insufficiently privileged Case cannot read the form or Timeline data.
Go race/vet and Timeline and cross-product Command HTTP plus engineering-kernel must pass on exact commit SHA.

rules: Strict tenant isolation and permission checking
